1: """Third-party proxy extension point.
2: 
3: External packages hook into the Headroom proxy at startup by declaring an
4: entry point in the ``headroom.proxy_extension`` group in their ``pyproject.toml``:
5: 
6:     [project.entry-points."headroom.proxy_extension"]
7:     my_extension = "my_pkg.extension:install"
8: 
9: Each ``install`` callable is invoked with the FastAPI ``app`` and the
10: ``ProxyConfig`` at app creation time, and is free to:
11: 
12:   * register ASGI middleware (``app.add_middleware(...)``)
13:   * add routes or health endpoints
14:   * mutate config
15:   * raise on license / environment failure to abort startup
16: 
17: OSS makes no assumptions about what extensions do. The interface is
18: deliberately minimal; extensions own the complexity behind it.
19: 
20: Reporting what an extension saved, and what it cost
21: ---------------------------------------------------
22: 
23: An extension that changes the bill should say so, or the operator sees a
24: different total with nothing to attribute it to. Two calls, both taking the
25: ASGI ``scope`` so they work from middleware — which runs outside the request
26: handler and has no other way in::
27: 
28:     from headroom.proxy.savings_attribution import (
29:         record_scope_savings, record_scope_timing,
30:     )
31: 
32:     record_scope_savings(scope, "my_extension", tokens=1200, usd=0.004)
33:     record_scope_timing(scope, "my_extension", elapsed_ms)
34: 
35: ``record_scope_savings`` takes ``tokens``, ``usd``, or both, so an extension
36: that saves money WITHOUT saving tokens — routing a request to a cheaper model,
37: say — can report a real number instead of a token count nobody saved. Pass
38: ``realized=False`` for a projection rather than a measured amount; the two are
39: kept apart everywhere they surface. Savings land on ``/stats`` under
40: ``savings.by_source``, on the dashboard as their own card, and in Prometheus as
41: ``headroom_savings_attributed_usd_total{source=...}``. **Attribution only** —
42: these rows explain the headline total, they are never added to it.
43: 
44: ``record_scope_timing`` is the other half of the trade: an extension's own
45: latency, which is otherwise invisible because ``overhead_ms`` is measured
46: inside the handler that the extension wraps. It lands in ``/stats`` under
47: ``pipeline_timing``, in the dashboard's Performance panel, and in
48: ``headroom_transform_timing_ms_*``, namespaced ``ext:<name>`` so it can never
49: collide with a built-in transform.
50: 
51: Both are bounded (32 sources, 16 stages), never raise, and never change a
52: response — telemetry from a plugin must not be able to break the request it is
53: describing.
54: 
55: **Extensions are opt-in.** Discovery enumerates every registered extension,
56: but ``install_all`` only invokes those explicitly enabled by the operator.
57: This protects users from silent behavior changes when a package they didn't
58: audit gets installed in the same environment (e.g., as a transitive dep).
59: 
60: Enabling extensions:
61: 
62:   * CLI:  ``headroom proxy --proxy-extension shield_enterprise,mypkg``
63:   * Env:  ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS=shield_enterprise,mypkg``
64:   * Wildcard: ``--proxy-extension '*'`` enables every discovered extension
65:     (use only when you trust everything in your environment).
66: 
67: Stability contract: this module is load-bearing for the Enterprise build and
68: any third-party extensions. Changes to the signature of ``install(app, config)``
69: or the entry-point group name require a deprecation cycle.
70: """
71: 
72: from __future__ import annotations
73: 
74: import importlib.metadata
75: import logging
76: import os
77: from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator
78: from typing import Any
79: 
80: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
81: 
82: ENTRY_POINT_GROUP = "headroom.proxy_extension"
83: ENV_VAR = "HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS"
84: 
85: ProxyExtension = Callable[[Any, Any], None]
86: """Signature: ``install(app: FastAPI, config: ProxyConfig) -> None``."""
87: 
88: 
89: def discover() -> Iterator[tuple[str, ProxyExtension]]:
90:     """Yield ``(name, install_callable)`` pairs for every registered extension.
91: 
92:     Entry-point load failures are logged and skipped — a broken third-party
93:     package must not prevent the proxy from starting. An extension that wants
94:     to fail-closed can raise from its ``install()``.
95:     """
96:     try:
97:         entries = importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=ENTRY_POINT_GROUP)
98:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — importlib.metadata can raise varied types
99:         log.debug("proxy extensions: entry-point enumeration failed: %s", exc)
100:         return
101:     for entry in entries:
102:         try:
103:             install = entry.load()
104:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
105:             log.warning("proxy extension %r failed to load: %s", entry.name, exc)
106:             continue
107:         yield entry.name, install
108: 
109: 
110: def _resolve_enabled(enabled: Iterable[str] | None) -> set[str]:
111:     """Resolve the set of enabled extension names.
112: 
113:     Precedence: explicit ``enabled`` argument > ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS``
114:     env var > empty (no extensions). Empty strings and whitespace are
115:     stripped. The literal ``*`` enables all discovered extensions.
116:     """
117:     raw: Iterable[str]
118:     if enabled is not None:
119:         raw = enabled
120:     else:
121:         raw = (os.environ.get(ENV_VAR) or "").split(",")
122:     out: set[str] = set()
123:     for n in raw:
124:         n = n.strip()
125:         if n:
126:             out.add(n)
127:     return out
128: 
129: 
130: def install_all(
131:     app: Any,
132:     config: Any,
133:     enabled: Iterable[str] | None = None,
134: ) -> list[str]:
135:     """Run only the explicitly-enabled extensions' ``install(app, config)``.
136: 
137:     Discovery still runs so we can log the universe of available extensions,
138:     but only those whose entry-point ``name`` is in ``enabled`` are invoked.
139:     The literal ``"*"`` in ``enabled`` is a wildcard that enables every
140:     discovered extension.
141: 
142:     Returns the names of successfully installed extensions. If an extension
143:     raises inside ``install()``, the exception propagates — this is the
144:     documented fail-closed signal (e.g., a license check failing should
145:     abort startup rather than silently run without protection).
146:     """
147:     enabled_set = _resolve_enabled(enabled)
148:     discovered = list(discover())
149:     discovered_names = [n for n, _ in discovered]
150: 
151:     if not enabled_set:
152:         if discovered_names:
153:             log.info(
154:                 "proxy extensions discovered but disabled (opt-in): %s. "
155:                 "Enable with --proxy-extension <name> or %s=<name1,name2>.",
156:                 ",".join(discovered_names),
157:                 ENV_VAR,
158:             )
159:         return []
160: 
161:     wildcard = "*" in enabled_set
162:     installed: list[str] = []
163:     for name, install in discovered:
164:         if not wildcard and name not in enabled_set:
165:             continue
166:         install(app, config)
167:         installed.append(name)
168:         log.info("proxy extension installed: %s", name)
169: 
170:     # Warn about names the user asked for that weren't found.
171:     if not wildcard:
172:         missing = enabled_set - set(discovered_names)
173:         if missing:
174:             log.warning(
175:                 "proxy extensions requested but not found: %s (available: %s)",
176:                 ",".join(sorted(missing)),
177:                 ",".join(discovered_names) or "<none>",
178:             )
179:     return installed

</content>

24: different total with nothing to attribute it to. Two calls, both taking the

26: handler and has no other way in::

28:     from headroom.proxy.savings_attribution import (
29:         record_scope_savings, record_scope_timing,
30:     )

36: that saves money WITHOUT saving tokens — routing a request to a cheaper model,
37: say — can report a real number instead of a token count nobody saved. Pass
38: ``realized=False`` for a projection rather than a measured amount; the two are
39: kept apart everywhere they surface. Savings land on ``/stats`` under
40: ``savings.by_source``, on the dashboard as their own card, and in Prometheus as
41: ``headroom_savings_attributed_usd_total{source=...}``. **Attribution only** —
42: these rows explain the headline total, they are never added to it.

45: latency, which is otherwise invisible because ``overhead_ms`` is measured
46: inside the handler that the extension wraps. It lands in ``/stats`` under
47: ``pipeline_timing``, in the dashboard's Performance panel, and in
48: ``headroom_transform_timing_ms_*``, namespaced ``ext:<name>`` so it can never
49: collide with a built-in transform.

52: response — telemetry from a plugin must not be able to break the request it is
53: describing.

56: but ``install_all`` only invokes those explicitly enabled by the operator.
57: This protects users from silent behavior changes when a package they didn't
58: audit gets installed in the same environment (e.g., as a transitive dep).

63:   * Env:  ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS=shield_enterprise,mypkg``
64:   * Wildcard: ``--proxy-extension '*'`` enables every discovered extension

68: any third-party extensions. Changes to the signature of ``install(app, config)``
69: or the entry-point group name require a deprecation cycle.

75: import logging
76: import os

78: from typing import Any

86: """Signature: ``install(app: FastAPI, config: ProxyConfig) -> None``."""

153:             log.info(
154:                 "proxy extensions discovered but disabled (opt-in): %s. "

158:             )

160: 
161:     wildcard = "*" in enabled_set

169:

1: """Third-party proxy extension point.
2: 
3: External packages hook into the Headroom proxy at startup by declaring an
4: entry point in the ``headroom.proxy_extension`` group in their ``pyproject.toml``:
5: 
6:     [project.entry-points."headroom.proxy_extension"]
7:     my_extension = "my_pkg.extension:install"
8: 
9: Each ``install`` callable is invoked with the FastAPI ``app`` and the
10: ``ProxyConfig`` at app creation time, and is free to:
11: 
12:   * register ASGI middleware (``app.add_middleware(...)``)
13:   * add routes or health endpoints
14:   * mutate config
15:   * raise on license / environment failure to abort startup
16: 
17: OSS makes no assumptions about what extensions do. The interface is
18: deliberately minimal; extensions own the complexity behind it.
19: 
20: Reporting what an extension saved, and what it cost
21: ---------------------------------------------------
22: 
23: An extension that changes the bill should say so, or the operator sees a
24: different total with nothing to attribute it to. Two calls, both taking the
25: ASGI ``scope`` so they work from middleware — which runs outside the request
26: handler and has no other way in::
27: 
28:     from headroom.proxy.savings_attribution import (
29:         record_scope_savings, record_scope_timing,
30:     )
31: 
32:     record_scope_savings(scope, "my_extension", tokens=1200, usd=0.004)
33:     record_scope_timing(scope, "my_extension", elapsed_ms)
34: 
35: ``record_scope_savings`` takes ``tokens``, ``usd``, or both, so an extension
36: that saves money WITHOUT saving tokens — routing a request to a cheaper model,
37: say — can report a real number instead of a token count nobody saved. Pass
38: ``realized=False`` for a projection rather than a measured amount; the two are
39: kept apart everywhere they surface. Savings land on ``/stats`` under
40: ``savings.by_source``, on the dashboard as their own card, and in Prometheus as
41: ``headroom_savings_attributed_usd_total{source=...}``. **Attribution only** —
42: these rows explain the headline total, they are never added to it.
43: 
44: ``record_scope_timing`` is the other half of the trade: an extension's own
45: latency, which is otherwise invisible because ``overhead_ms`` is measured
46: inside the handler that the extension wraps. It lands in ``/stats`` under
47: ``pipeline_timing``, in the dashboard's Performance panel, and in
48: ``headroom_transform_timing_ms_*``, namespaced ``ext:<name>`` so it can never
49: collide with a built-in transform.
50: 
51: Both are bounded (32 sources, 16 stages), never raise, and never change a
52: response — telemetry from a plugin must not be able to break the request it is
53: describing.
54: 
55: **Extensions are opt-in.** Discovery enumerates every registered extension,
56: but ``install_all`` only invokes those explicitly enabled by the operator.
57: This protects users from silent behavior changes when a package they didn't
58: audit gets installed in the same environment (e.g., as a transitive dep).
59: 
60: Enabling extensions:
61: 
62:   * CLI:  ``headroom proxy --proxy-extension shield_enterprise,mypkg``
63:   * Env:  ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS=shield_enterprise,mypkg``
64:   * Wildcard: ``--proxy-extension '*'`` enables every discovered extension
65:     (use only when you trust everything in your environment).
66: 
67: Stability contract: this module is load-bearing for the Enterprise build and
68: any third-party extensions. Changes to the signature of ``install(app, config)``
69: or the entry-point group name require a deprecation cycle.
70: """
71: 
72: from __future__ import annotations
73: 
74: import importlib.metadata
75: import logging
76: import os
77: from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator
78: from typing import Any
79: 
80: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
81: 
82: ENTRY_POINT_GROUP = "headroom.proxy_extension"
83: ENV_VAR = "HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS"
84: 
85: ProxyExtension = Callable[[Any, Any], None]
86: """Signature: ``install(app: FastAPI, config: ProxyConfig) -> None``."""
87: 
88: 
89: def discover() -> Iterator[tuple[str, ProxyExtension]]:
90:     """Yield ``(name, install_callable)`` pairs for every registered extension.
91: 
92:     Entry-point load failures are logged and skipped — a broken third-party
93:     package must not prevent the proxy from starting. An extension that wants
94:     to fail-closed can raise from its ``install()``.
95:     """
96:     try:
97:         entries = importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=ENTRY_POINT_GROUP)
98:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — importlib.metadata can raise varied types
99:         log.debug("proxy extensions: entry-point enumeration failed: %s", exc)
100:         return
101:     for entry in entries:
102:         try:
103:             install = entry.load()
104:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
105:             log.warning("proxy extension %r failed to load: %s", entry.name, exc)
106:             continue
107:         yield entry.name, install
108: 
109: 
110: def _resolve_enabled(enabled: Iterable[str] | None) -> set[str]:
111:     """Resolve the set of enabled extension names.
112: 
113:     Precedence: explicit ``enabled`` argument > ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS``
114:     env var > empty (no extensions). Empty strings and whitespace are
115:     stripped. The literal ``*`` enables all discovered extensions.
116:     """
117:     raw: Iterable[str]
118:     if enabled is not None:
119:         raw = enabled
120:     else:
121:         raw = (os.environ.get(ENV_VAR) or "").split(",")
122:     out: set[str] = set()
123:     for n in raw:
124:         n = n.strip()
125:         if n:
126:             out.add(n)
127:     return out
128: 
129: 
130: def install_all(
131:     app: Any,
132:     config: Any,
133:     enabled: Iterable[str] | None = None,
134: ) -> list[str]:
135:     """Run only the explicitly-enabled extensions' ``install(app, config)``.
136: 
137:     Discovery still runs so we can log the universe of available extensions,
138:     but only those whose entry-point ``name`` is in ``enabled`` are invoked.
139:     The literal ``"*"`` in ``enabled`` is a wildcard that enables every
140:     discovered extension.
141: 
142:     Returns the names of successfully installed extensions. If an extension
143:     raises inside ``install()``, the exception propagates — this is the
144:     documented fail-closed signal (e.g., a license check failing should
145:     abort startup rather than silently run without protection).
146:     """
147:     enabled_set = _resolve_enabled(enabled)
148:     discovered = list(discover())
149:     discovered_names = [n for n, _ in discovered]
150: 
151:     if not enabled_set:
152:         if discovered_names:
153:             log.info(
154:                 "proxy extensions discovered but disabled (opt-in): %s. "
155:                 "Enable with --proxy-extension <name> or %s=<name1,name2>.",
156:                 ",".join(discovered_names),
157:                 ENV_VAR,
158:             )
159:         return []
160: 
161:     wildcard = "*" in enabled_set
162:     installed: list[str] = []
163:     for name, install in discovered:
164:         if not wildcard and name not in enabled_set:
165:             continue
166:         install(app, config)
167:         installed.append(name)
168:         log.info("proxy extension installed: %s", name)
169: 
170:     # Warn about names the user asked for that weren't found.
171:     if not wildcard:
172:         missing = enabled_set - set(discovered_names)
173:         if missing:
174:             log.warning(
175:                 "proxy extensions requested but not found: %s (available: %s)",
176:                 ",".join(sorted(missing)),
177:                 ",".join(discovered_names) or "<none>",
178:             )
179:     return installed

6:     [project.entry-points."headroom.proxy_extension"]
7:     my_extension = "my_pkg.extension:install"
8: 
9: Each ``install`` callable is invoked with the FastAPI ``app`` and the
10: ``ProxyConfig`` at app creation time, and is free to:
11: 
12:   * register ASGI middleware (``app.add_middleware(...)``)
13:   * add routes or health endpoints
14:   * mutate config
15:   * raise on license / environment failure to abort startup
16: 
17: OSS makes no assumptions about what extensions do. The interface is
18: deliberately minimal; extensions own the complexity behind it.
19: 
20: Reporting what an extension saved, and what it cost
21: ---------------------------------------------------
22: 
23: An extension that changes the bill should say so, or the operator sees a
24: different total with nothing to attribute it to. Two calls, both taking the
25: ASGI ``scope`` so they work from middleware — which runs outside the request
26: handler and has no other way in::
27: 
28:     from headroom.proxy.savings_attribution import (
29:         record_scope_savings, record_scope_timing,
30:     )
31: 
32:     record_scope_savings(scope, "my_extension", tokens=1200, usd=0.004)
33:     record_scope_timing(scope, "my_extension", elapsed_ms)
34: 
35: ``record_scope_savings`` takes ``tokens``, ``usd``, or both, so an extension
36: that saves money WITHOUT saving tokens — routing a request to a cheaper model,
37: say — can report a real number instead of a token count nobody saved. Pass
38: ``realized=False`` for a projection rather than a measured amount; the two are
39: kept apart everywhere they surface. Savings land on ``/stats`` under
40: ``savings.by_source``, on the dashboard as their own card, and in Prometheus as
41: ``headroom_savings_attributed_usd_total{source=...}``. **Attribution only** —
42: these rows explain the headline total, they are never added to it.
43: 
44: ``record_scope_timing`` is the other half of the trade: an extension's own
45: latency, which is otherwise invisible because ``overhead_ms`` is measured
46: inside the handler that the extension wraps. It lands in ``/stats`` under
47: ``pipeline_timing``, in the dashboard's Performance panel, and in
48: ``headroom_transform_timing_ms_*``, namespaced ``ext:<name>`` so it can never
49: collide with a built-in transform.
50: 
51: Both are bounded (32 sources, 16 stages), never raise, and never change a
52: response — telemetry from a plugin must not be able to break the request it is
53: describing.
54: 
55: **Extensions are opt-in.** Discovery enumerates every registered extension,
56: but ``install_all`` only invokes those explicitly enabled by the operator.
57: This protects users from silent behavior changes when a package they didn't
58: audit gets installed in the same environment (e.g., as a transitive dep).
59: 
60: Enabling extensions:
61: 
62:   * CLI:  ``headroom proxy --proxy-extension shield_enterprise,mypkg``
63:   * Env:  ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS=shield_enterprise,mypkg``
64:   * Wildcard: ``--proxy-extension '*'`` enables every discovered extension
65:     (use only when you trust everything in your environment).
66: 
67: Stability contract: this module is load-bearing for the Enterprise build and
68: any third-party extensions. Changes to the signature of ``install(app, config)``
69: or the entry-point group name require a deprecation cycle.
70: """
71: 
72: from __future__ import annotations
73: 
74: import importlib.metadata
75: import logging
76: import os
77: from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator
78: from typing import Any
79: 
80: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
81: 
82: ENTRY_POINT_GROUP = "headroom.proxy_extension"
83: ENV_VAR = "HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS"
84: 
85: ProxyExtension = Callable[[Any, Any], None]
86: """Signature: ``install(app: FastAPI, config: ProxyConfig) -> None``."""
87: 
88: 
89: def discover() -> Iterator[tuple[str, ProxyExtension]]:
90:     """Yield ``(name, install_callable)`` pairs for every registered extension.
91: 
92:     Entry-point load failures are logged and skipped — a broken third-party
93:     package must not prevent the proxy from starting. An extension that wants
94:     to fail-closed can raise from its ``install()``.
95:     """
96:     try:
97:         entries = importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=ENTRY_POINT_GROUP)
98:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — importlib.metadata can raise varied types
99:         log.debug("proxy extensions: entry-point enumeration failed: %s", exc)
100:         return
101:     for entry in entries:
102:         try:
103:             install = entry.load()
104:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
105:             log.warning("proxy extension %r failed to load: %s", entry.name, exc)
106:             continue
107:         yield entry.name, install
108: 
109: 
110: def _resolve_enabled(enabled: Iterable[str] | None) -> set[str]:
111:     """Resolve the set of enabled extension names.
112: 
113:     Precedence: explicit ``enabled`` argument > ``HEADROOM_PROXY_EXTENSIONS``
114:     env var > empty (no extensions). Empty strings and whitespace are
115:     stripped. The literal ``*`` enables all discovered extensions.
116:     """
117:     raw: Iterable[str]
118:     if enabled is not None:
119:         raw = enabled
120:     else:
121:         raw = (os.environ.get(ENV_VAR) or "").split(",")
122:     out: set[str] = set()
123:     for n in raw:
124:         n = n.strip()
125:         if n:
126:             out.add(n)
127:     return out
128: 
129: 
130: def install_all(
131:     app: Any,
132:     config: Any,
133:     enabled: Iterable[str] | None = None,
134: ) -> list[str]:
135:     """Run only the explicitly-enabled extensions' ``install(app, config)``.
136: 
137:     Discovery still runs so we can log the universe of available extensions,
138:     but only those whose entry-point ``name`` is in ``enabled`` are invoked.
139:     The literal ``"*"`` in ``enabled`` is a wildcard that enables every
140:     discovered extension.
141: 
142:     Returns the names of successfully installed extensions. If an extension
143:     raises inside ``install()``, the exception propagates — this is the
144:     documented fail-closed signal (e.g., a license check failing should
145:     abort startup rather than silently run without protection).
146:     """
147:     enabled_set = _resolve_enabled(enabled)
148:     discovered = list(discover())
149:     discovered_names = [n for n, _ in discovered]
150: 
151:     if not enabled_set:
152:         if discovered_names:
153:             log.info(
154:                 "proxy extensions discovered but disabled (opt-in): %s. "
155:                 "Enable with --proxy-extension <name> or %s=<name1,name2>.",
156:                 ",".join(discovered_names),
157:                 ENV_VAR,
158:             )
159:         return []
160: 
161:     wildcard = "*" in enabled_set
162:     installed: list[str] = []
163:     for name, install in discovered:
164:         if not wildcard and name not in enabled_set:
165:             continue
166:         install(app, config)
167:         installed.append(name)
168:         log.info("proxy extension installed: %s", name)
169: 
170:     # Warn about names the user asked for that weren't found.
171:     if not wildcard:
172:         missing = enabled_set - set(discovered_names)
173:         if missing:
174:             log.warning(
175:                 "proxy extensions requested but not found: %s (available: %s)",
176:                 ",".join(sorted(missing)),
177:                 ",".join(discovered_names) or "<none>",
178:             )
179:     return installed

634:         event loop (~seconds). json.dumps itself is cheap; count_text over the
635:         whole string is the cost, so its input must stay bounded for oversized
636:         blobs.

632:     def test_oversized_tool_blob_count_text_is_bounded(self, monkeypatch):
633:         """Regression: count_text over a multi-megabyte serialized blob froze the
634:         event loop (~seconds). json.dumps itself is cheap; count_text over the
635:         whole string is the cost, so its input must stay bounded for oversized
636:         blobs.
637:         """

639:         sizes: list[int] = []

630:     """Oversized tool blobs are token-estimated without serializing them in full."""

632:     def test_oversized_tool_blob_count_text_is_bounded(self, monkeypatch):
633:         """Regression: count_text over a multi-megabyte serialized blob froze the
634:         event loop (~seconds). json.dumps itself is cheap; count_text over the
635:         whole string is the cost, so its input must stay bounded for oversized
636:         blobs.
637:         """
638:         tok = EstimatingTokenCounter()
639:         sizes: list[int] = []
640:         real_count_text = tok.count_text
641: 
642:         def spy(text):
643:             sizes.append(len(text))
644:             return real_count_text(text)
645: 
646:         monkeypatch.setattr(tok, "count_text", spy)
647:         messages = [
648:             {
649:                 "role": "user",
650:                 "content": [
651:                     {"type": "tool_result", "content": {"small": "x"}},
652:                     {"type": "tool_result", "content": {"data": "A" * 4_000_000}},
653:                 ],
654:             }
655:         ]
656:         tok.count_messages(messages)
657: 
658:         assert sizes, "count_text should be exercised"
659:         # the 4 MB blob must never be counted whole — only its bounded sample
660:         assert max(sizes) <= tok.SAMPLE_CHARS + tok.SAMPLE_CHUNK
661:

663:         """Small blobs stay exact; large ones track the active counter, not a flat ratio."""
664:         import json
665: 
666:         tok = EstimatingTokenCounter(chars_per_token=3.5)  # Claude-like ratio
667:         small = {"k": "v"}
668:         assert tok._count_serialized(small) == tok.count_text(json.dumps(small))
669: 
670:         # Within 10% of the exact full count (a flat ratio would be ~15% off for 3.5).
671:         big = {"k": "A" * 200_000}
672:         exact = tok.count_text(json.dumps(big))
673:         assert abs(tok._count_serialized(big) - exact) / exact < 0.10

1: """Base classes for tokenizer implementations.
2: 
3: Defines the TokenCounter protocol and BaseTokenizer class that all
4: tokenizer backends must implement.
5: """
6: 
7: from __future__ import annotations
8: 
9: import json
10: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
11: from collections.abc import Callable
12: from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
13: 
14: #: Cap on the serialized form of a non-string tool-call field. A malformed
15: #: upstream can put an arbitrarily large object where a JSON string belongs;
16: #: serializing it unbounded would turn a token *estimate* into a multi-megabyte
17: #: encode. Truncating keeps the estimate finite and the request alive.
18: _MAX_COERCED_FIELD_CHARS = 200_000
19: 
20: #: Admission policy for :class:`TokenCountCache`. These bound memory only — they
21: #: never change a returned count, so they are not a behavioural threshold.
22: #: Strings below the floor encode in microseconds, so caching them would only
23: #: evict the large entries that the cache exists for.
24: _COUNT_CACHE_MIN_CHARS = 256
25: _COUNT_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 4096
26: _COUNT_CACHE_MAX_CHARS = 8_000_000
27: 
28: 
29: class TokenCountCache:
30:     """Exact memo for ``count_text``.
31: 
32:     ``count_text`` is a pure function of its text, so replaying a stored count is
33:     value-identical. That is the whole safety argument: the result is the same
34:     integer, which is why this is safe even at the call sites whose count feeds a
35:     routing decision (``context_pressure`` -> ``min_ratio``) rather than a log line.
36: 
37:     Keyed on the text itself rather than a hash. A hash collision here would hand
38:     back the wrong count for real content and silently change what gets
39:     compressed; the counts are too load-bearing to trade correctness for a
40:     smaller key. The price is holding the strings, so entries *and* total
41:     characters are capped.
42: 
43:     No lock: ``dict`` get/set/clear are atomic under the GIL, and the pipeline
44:     runs on a thread pool. An LRU would need ``move_to_end``, which is not
45:     atomic — hence clear-on-full rather than eviction. A cleared cache costs one
46:     re-encode, never a wrong answer.
47:     """
48: 
49:     __slots__ = ("_chars", "_counts", "_max_chars", "_max_entries", "_min_chars")
50: 
51:     def __init__(
52:         self,
53:         *,
54:         min_chars: int = _COUNT_CACHE_MIN_CHARS,
55:         max_entries: int = _COUNT_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES,
56:         max_chars: int = _COUNT_CACHE_MAX_CHARS,
57:     ) -> None:
58:         self._counts: dict[str, int] = {}
59:         self._chars = 0
60:         self._min_chars = min_chars
61:         self._max_entries = max_entries
62:         self._max_chars = max_chars
63: 
64:     def get(self, text: str) -> int | None:
65:         """Return the stored count for *text*, or None."""
66:         return self._counts.get(text)
67: 
68:     def put(self, text: str, count: int) -> None:
69:         """Store *count* for *text* if it is worth caching."""
70:         if len(text) < self._min_chars:
71:             return
72:         if len(self._counts) >= self._max_entries or self._chars >= self._max_chars:
73:             self._counts.clear()
74:             self._chars = 0
75:         self._counts[text] = count
76:         self._chars += len(text)
77: 
78:     def clear(self) -> None:
79:         self._counts.clear()
80:         self._chars = 0
81: 
82: 
83: def coerce_countable_text(value: Any) -> str:
84:     """Return *value* as text safe to pass to ``count_text``.
85: 
86:     Tool-call fields (``function.name``, ``function.arguments``, ``id``) are
87:     strings per the OpenAI spec, but OpenAI-compatible upstreams do emit
88:     ``None`` or a raw object there. Passing those straight to
89:     ``tiktoken.encode()`` raises ``TypeError: expected string or buffer``, which
90:     failed the whole compression with a 503 — and kept failing on every later
91:     request, because the malformed message stays in conversation history.
92: 
93:     ``None`` counts as nothing; dicts/lists are JSON-serialized so an object
94:     ``arguments`` is priced roughly like the JSON string it should have been;
95:     anything else falls back to ``str()``.
96:     """
97:     if isinstance(value, str):
98:         return value
99:     if value is None:
100:         return ""
101:     if isinstance(value, dict | list | tuple):
102:         try:
103:             text = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
104:         except (TypeError, ValueError):
105:             text = str(value)
106:     else:
107:         text = str(value)
108:     return text[:_MAX_COERCED_FIELD_CHARS]
109:

112: class TokenCounter(Protocol):
113:     """Protocol for token counting implementations.
114: 
115:     Any class implementing this protocol can be used with Headroom
116:     for token counting. This allows integration with various
117:     tokenizer backends (tiktoken, HuggingFace, custom, etc.).
118:     """
119: 
120:     def count_text(self, text: str) -> int:
121:         """Count tokens in a text string.
122: 
123:         Args:
124:             text: The text to count tokens for.
125: 
126:         Returns:
127:             Number of tokens in the text.
128:         """
129:         ...
130: 
131:     def count_messages(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
132:         """Count tokens in a list of chat messages.
133: 
134:         Args:
135:             messages: List of message dicts with 'role' and 'content'.
136: 
137:         Returns:
138:             Total token count including message overhead.
139:         """
140:         ...
141:

143: class BaseTokenizer(ABC):
144:     """Abstract base class for tokenizer implementations.
145: 
146:     Provides common functionality for counting messages while
147:     requiring subclasses to implement text tokenization.
148:     """
149: 
150:     # Token overhead per message (role, formatting, etc.)
151:     # Override in subclasses for model-specific overhead
152:     MESSAGE_OVERHEAD = 4
153:     REPLY_OVERHEAD = 3  # Assistant reply start tokens
154: 
155:     # Oversized-blob token estimation (see _count_serialized). Serializing a blob
156:     # is cheap; running count_text over the whole multi-megabyte string is what
157:     # blocks the proxy event loop, so a large blob is counted from an even-spread
158:     # sample of the serialized string, scaled by length.
159:     LARGE_BLOB_CHARS = 50_000  # above this serialized size, sample instead of full count
160:     SAMPLE_CHARS = 20_000  # total characters fed to count_text for an oversized blob
161:     SAMPLE_CHUNK = 2_000  # size of each evenly-spaced chunk in that sample
162: 
163:     @abstractmethod
164:     def count_text(self, text: str) -> int:
165:         """Count tokens in a text string. Must be implemented by subclasses."""
166:         pass
167: 
168:     def count_message(self, message: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
169:         """Count tokens in a single message.
170: 
171:         Args:
172:             message: A message dict with 'role' and 'content'.
173: 
174:         Returns:
175:             Token count for this message.
176:         """
177:         return self.count_messages([message]) - self.REPLY_OVERHEAD
178: 
179:     def count_messages(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
180:         """Count tokens in a list of chat messages.
181: 
182:         Uses OpenAI-style message counting as the baseline, which
183:         works well for most models.
184: 
185:         Args:
186:             messages: List of message dicts.
187: 
188:         Returns:
189:             Total token count.
190:         """
191:         total = 0
192: 
193:         for message in messages:
194:             # Base message overhead
195:             total += self.MESSAGE_OVERHEAD
196: 
197:             # Count role
198:             role = message.get("role", "")
199:             total += self.count_text(role)
200: 
201:             # Count content
202:             content = message.get("content")
203:             if content is not None:
204:                 if isinstance(content, str):
205:                     total += self.count_text(content)
206:                 elif isinstance(content, list):
207:                     # Multi-part content (images, tool results, etc.)
208:                     total += self._count_content_parts(content)
209: 
210:             # Count tool calls
211:             tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
212:             if tool_calls:
213:                 total += self._count_tool_calls(tool_calls)
214: 
215:             # Count function call (legacy)
216:             function_call = message.get("function_call")
217:             if function_call:
218:                 total += self._count_function_call(function_call)
219: 
220:             # Count name field
221:             name = message.get("name")
222:             if name:
223:                 total += self.count_text(name)
224:                 total += 1  # Name field overhead
225: 
226:         # Reply start overhead
227:         total += self.REPLY_OVERHEAD
228: 
229:         return total
230: 
231:     def _count_content_parts(self, parts: list[Any]) -> int:
232:         """Count tokens in multi-part content.
233: 
234:         Handles both Anthropic format ({"type": "text", "text": "..."})
235:         and Strands SDK format ({"text": "..."} without "type" field).
236:         """
237:         total = 0
238:         for part in parts:
239:             if isinstance(part, dict):
240:                 part_type = part.get("type", "")
241: 
242:                 if part_type == "text":
243:                     total += self.count_text(part.get("text", ""))
244:                 elif part_type in ("image_url", "image", "input_image"):
245:                     # Images are NOT tokenized as text — they have a pixel-based cost.
246:                     # Anthropic: tokens = (width * height) / 750, max ~1600 after resize.
247:                     # OpenAI: similar tile-based calculation, ~765 tokens for high-detail.
248:                     # We use 1600 as a conservative estimate (max after auto-resize).
249:                     # This prevents the base64 blob from being json.dumps'd and counted
250:                     # as text tokens (1MB image = ~330K fake tokens without this).
251:                     total += 1600
252:                 elif part_type in ("input_audio", "audio"):
253:                     # Audio has fixed token cost, not tokenized as text
254:                     total += 200
255:                 elif part_type == "tool_result":
256:                     content = part.get("content", "")
257:                     if isinstance(content, str):
258:                         total += self.count_text(content)
259:                     elif isinstance(content, list):
260:                         # Recurse into nested blocks (matching the Strands
261:                         # toolResult branch below). A tool that returns an image
262:                         # nests a base64 block here; serializing it would price
263:                         # the ~KB/MB base64 string as text — a 50-200x overcount
264:                         # (a screenshot reads as tens of thousands of tokens).
265:                         total += self._count_content_parts(content)
266:                     else:
267:                         total += self._count_serialized(content)
268:                 elif part_type == "tool_use":
269:                     total += self.count_text(part.get("name", ""))
270:                     total += self._count_serialized(part.get("input", {}))
271:                 elif not part_type and "text" in part:
272:                     # Strands SDK format: {"text": "..."} without "type" field
273:                     total += self.count_text(part["text"])
274:                 elif not part_type and "toolUse" in part:
275:                     # Strands SDK tool_use: {"toolUse": {"name": ..., "input": ...}}
276:                     tool_use = part["toolUse"]
277:                     total += self.count_text(tool_use.get("name", ""))
278:                     total += self._count_serialized(tool_use.get("input", {}))
279:                 elif not part_type and "toolResult" in part:
280:                     # Strands SDK tool_result: {"toolResult": {"content": [...]}}
281:                     tool_result = part["toolResult"]
282:                     tr_content = tool_result.get("content", [])
283:                     if isinstance(tr_content, str):
284:                         total += self.count_text(tr_content)
285:                     elif isinstance(tr_content, list):
286:                         # Recurse into nested content blocks
287:                         total += self._count_content_parts(tr_content)
288:                     else:
289:                         total += self._count_serialized(tr_content)
290:                 elif not part_type and "reasoningContent" in part:
291:                     # Strands SDK reasoning: {"reasoningContent": {"reasoningText": {"text": "..."}}}
292:                     # This is actual text — count it precisely.
293:                     reasoning = part["reasoningContent"]
294:                     reasoning_text = reasoning.get("reasoningText", {})
295:                     if isinstance(reasoning_text, dict):
296:                         total += self.count_text(reasoning_text.get("text", ""))
297:                     elif isinstance(reasoning_text, str):
298:                         total += self.count_text(reasoning_text)
299:                 elif not part_type and "document" in part:
300:                     # Strands SDK document: {"document": {"source": {"bytes": ...}}}
301:                     # Provider internally extracts text from PDF/DOCX then tokenizes.
302:                     # Accurate counting would require a PDF parser — instead we use
303:                     # the Anthropic documented estimate of ~1500 tokens per page,
304:                     # with ~3KB of PDF per page as a rough heuristic.
305:                     doc = part["document"]
306:                     source = doc.get("source", {})
307:                     doc_bytes = source.get("bytes", b"")
308:                     if isinstance(doc_bytes, bytes | bytearray):
309:                         estimated_pages = max(1, len(doc_bytes) // 3000)
310:                         total += estimated_pages * 1500
311:                     else:
312:                         total += self.count_text(str(doc_bytes))
313:                 elif not part_type and "image" in part:
314:                     # Strands SDK image: {"image": {"source": {"bytes": ...}}}
315:                     # Anthropic formula: tokens = (width * height) / 750.
316:                     # Decode with Pillow for exact count; fall back to estimate.
317:                     total += self._estimate_image_tokens(part["image"])
318:                 elif not part_type and "video" in part:
319:                     # Strands SDK video: provider samples ~1 fps, each frame costs
320:                     # image tokens. We can't decode frames without heavy deps, so
321:                     # estimate from byte size assuming ~30KB per frame, ~1000 tokens
322:                     # per frame (average image).
323:                     vid = part["video"]
324:                     source = vid.get("source", {})
325:                     vid_bytes = source.get("bytes", b"")
326:                     if isinstance(vid_bytes, bytes | bytearray):
327:                         frames = max(1, len(vid_bytes) // 30000)
328:                         total += frames * 1000
329:                     else:
330:                         total += 3200
331:                 else:
332:                     # Unknown type - estimate from JSON
333:                     total += self._count_serialized(part)
334:             elif isinstance(part, str):
335:                 total += self.count_text(part)
336: 
337:         return total
338: 
339:     def _count_serialized(self, obj: Any) -> int:
340:         """Count tokens for a non-string content blob.
341: 
342:         Small blobs are counted exactly. For an oversized one, run ``count_text``
343:         over an even-spread sample of the serialized string and scale by length.
344:         Serializing is cheap; ``count_text`` over the whole multi-megabyte string
345:         is what blocks the request path, so its input is bounded here. The even
346:         spread keeps the sample representative (a single slice would skew the scale
347:         high), and bounding the count biases the estimate slightly low — the safe
348:         direction. Fails open. Mirrors the image and document guards above.
349:         """
350:         try:
351:             s = json.dumps(obj)
352:         except Exception:
353:             # fail-open: nominal estimate when obj isn't JSON-serializable
354:             return self.LARGE_BLOB_CHARS // 4
355:         if len(s) <= self.LARGE_BLOB_CHARS:
356:             return self.count_text(s)
357:         chunks = max(1, self.SAMPLE_CHARS // self.SAMPLE_CHUNK)
358:         step = len(s) / chunks
359:         sample = "".join(
360:             s[int(i * step) : int(i * step) + self.SAMPLE_CHUNK] for i in range(chunks)
361:         )
362:         return int(self.count_text(sample) * len(s) / len(sample))
363: 
364:     @staticmethod
365:     def _estimate_image_tokens(image_data: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
366:         """Estimate tokens for an image using Anthropic's formula: (w*h)/750.
367: 
368:         Tries to decode dimensions with Pillow. Falls back to a conservative
369:         estimate based on byte size.
370:         """
371:         source = image_data.get("source", {})
372:         img_bytes = source.get("bytes", b"")
373: 
374:         if isinstance(img_bytes, bytes | bytearray) and len(img_bytes) > 0:
375:             try:
376:                 import io
377: 
378:                 from PIL import Image
379: 
380:                 img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(img_bytes))
381:                 w, h = img.size
382:                 # Anthropic resizes to fit 1568x1568 max
383:                 max_dim = 1568
384:                 if w > max_dim or h > max_dim:
385:                     scale = max_dim / max(w, h)
386:                     w, h = int(w * scale), int(h * scale)
387:                 return max(100, (w * h) // 750)
388:             except Exception:
389:                 pass
390: 
391:         # Fallback: estimate from byte size.
392:         # Typical screenshot: ~200KB ≈ 1200x800 ≈ 1280 tokens
393:         if isinstance(img_bytes, bytes | bytearray):

461: class _DelegatingBlockCounter(BaseTokenizer):
462:     """Adapter exposing :meth:`BaseTokenizer._count_content_parts` to non-subclasses.
463: 
464:     The provider token counters in ``headroom/providers/`` are not
465:     ``BaseTokenizer`` subclasses, and each grew its own shortened content-block
466:     walker that handled only the shapes its provider was expected to send. The
467:     result was that every one of them priced most modern blocks at ~0: measured
468:     on a 6,800-char block, ``OpenAITokenCounter`` returned 8 tokens for
469:     ``tool_result``/``thinking``/``document``/``mcp_tool_result`` and — its own
470:     Responses shapes — ``output_text``/``refusal``; ``AnthropicTokenCounter``
471:     returned 7 for ``thinking``/``document``, which are Anthropic's own.
472: 
473:     Rather than add a fifth partial walker, this lets them borrow the audited one.
474:     It is image-safe (base64 blobs get a pixel-based estimate instead of being
475:     serialized and priced as text) and bounds oversized blobs, which a naive
476:     ``count_text(str(block))`` catch-all does not.
477:     """
478: 
479:     __slots__ = ("_count_text_fn",)
480: 
481:     def __init__(self, count_text_fn: Callable[[str], int]) -> None:
482:         self._count_text_fn = count_text_fn
483: 
484:     def count_text(self, text: str) -> int:
485:         return self._count_text_fn(text)

1: """Tiktoken-based token counter for OpenAI models.
2: 
3: Tiktoken is OpenAI's fast BPE tokenizer used by GPT models.
4: It supports multiple encodings:
5: - cl100k_base: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, text-embedding-ada-002
6: - o200k_base: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini
7: - p50k_base: Codex models, text-davinci-002/003
8: - r50k_base: GPT-3 models (davinci, curie, etc.)
9: """

11: from __future__ import annotations
12: 
13: import logging
14: import os
15: import threading
16: from functools import lru_cache
17: from typing import Any

19: from .base import BaseTokenizer, TokenCountCache, coerce_countable_text

24: class TiktokenLoadError(RuntimeError):
25:     """Raised when a tiktoken encoding can't be loaded in time.
26: 
27:     tiktoken downloads its BPE vocab on first use via ``requests.get`` with no
28:     timeout, so a stalled/firewalled connection can block indefinitely. We bound
29:     that load and raise this instead, so callers fall back to estimation rather
30:     than hanging the request (see GH #956).
31:     """
32: 
33: 
34: # Encoding names whose bounded load already timed out — don't block on them again.
35: _load_failed: set[str] = set()
36: 
37: 
38: def _load_timeout_seconds() -> float:
39:     try:
40:         return float(os.environ.get("HEADROOM_TIKTOKEN_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "10"))
41:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
42:         return 10.0

48:     "gpt-4o": "o200k_base",
49:     "gpt-4o-mini": "o200k_base",

55:     "o1": "o200k_base",
56:     "o1-mini": "o200k_base",
57:     "o1-preview": "o200k_base",
58:     "o3-mini": "o200k_base",

60:     "gpt-4": "cl100k_base",

106: @lru_cache(maxsize=8)
107: def _get_encoding(encoding_name: str):
108:     """Get a tiktoken encoding, cached for performance.
109: 
110:     Bounded by ``HEADROOM_TIKTOKEN_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` (default 10s): tiktoken's
111:     vocab download has no network timeout, so we run the load on a worker thread
112:     and raise :class:`TiktokenLoadError` if it doesn't finish in time, letting
113:     callers fall back to estimation rather than hang the request (GH #956). The
114:     first timed-out encoding is remembered so later calls fail fast instead of
115:     re-blocking on every request.
116:     """
117:     import tiktoken
118: 
119:     if encoding_name in _load_failed:
120:         raise TiktokenLoadError(f"tiktoken encoding {encoding_name!r} previously failed to load")
121: 
122:     box: dict[str, Any] = {}
123: 
124:     def _load() -> None:
125:         try:
126:             box["enc"] = tiktoken.get_encoding(encoding_name)
127:         except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - re-raised in the calling thread
128:             box["err"] = exc
129: 
130:     worker = threading.Thread(target=_load, name=f"tiktoken-load-{encoding_name}", daemon=True)
131:     worker.start()
132:     worker.join(_load_timeout_seconds())
133: 
134:     if worker.is_alive():
135:         _load_failed.add(encoding_name)
136:         logger.warning(
137:             "tiktoken encoding %r did not load within %.1fs (likely a stalled vocab "
138:             "download); falling back to token estimation. Pre-populate TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR "
139:             "or tune HEADROOM_TIKTOKEN_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.",
140:             encoding_name,
141:             _load_timeout_seconds(),
142:         )
143:         raise TiktokenLoadError(f"tiktoken encoding {encoding_name!r} load timed out")
144:     if "err" in box:
145:         raise box["err"]
146:     return box["enc"]

149: def load_encoding(encoding_name: str) -> Any:
150:     """Public, bounded tiktoken-encoding loader.
151: 
152:     Returns the tiktoken encoding, or raises :class:`TiktokenLoadError` if the
153:     vocab can't be loaded within the timeout (see :func:`_get_encoding`, GH #956).
154:     """
155:     return _get_encoding(encoding_name)

158: def get_encoding_for_model(model: str) -> str:
159:     """Get the tiktoken encoding name for a model.
160: 
161:     Args:
162:         model: Model name (e.g., 'gpt-4o', 'gpt-3.5-turbo').
163: 
164:     Returns:
165:         Encoding name (e.g., 'o200k_base', 'cl100k_base').
166:     """
167:     # Case-insensitive: TokenizerRegistry lowercases only its *cache key*, then
168:     # constructs the counter from the caller's original string. An uppercase
169:     # deployment name ("GPT-4o", routine on Azure) therefore arrived here
170:     # verbatim, matched no prefix, and silently took DEFAULT_ENCODING -- so the
171:     # encoding a model got depended on the casing of whichever request warmed
172:     # the cache first, and flipped across restarts.
173:     model = model.lower()
174: 
175:     # Direct lookup
176:     if model in MODEL_TO_ENCODING:
177:         return MODEL_TO_ENCODING[model]
178: 
179:     # Try prefix matching for versioned models. Ordered most-specific first
180:     # so that, e.g., "gpt-4o-*" resolves before "gpt-4-*". Each prefix maps
181:     # directly to its encoding: scanning MODEL_TO_ENCODING for the first key
182:     # that merely starts with the prefix is order-dependent and wrong — the
183:     # "gpt-4" prefix would match the "gpt-4o" dict entry first and return
184:     # o200k_base instead of cl100k_base for unknown gpt-4 snapshots.
185:     for prefix, encoding in (
186:         ("gpt-4o", "o200k_base"),
187:         # gpt-4.1 / gpt-4.5 use o200k_base and MUST precede the "gpt-4" prefix,
188:         # which they would otherwise match and be mis-encoded as cl100k_base.
189:         ("gpt-4.1", "o200k_base"),
190:         ("gpt-4.5", "o200k_base"),
191:         # gpt-5 uses o200k_base. Without this it fell through to the
192:         # cl100k_base default, over-counting CJK by ~33%.
193:         ("gpt-5", "o200k_base"),
194:         ("gpt-4-turbo", "cl100k_base"),
195:         ("gpt-4", "cl100k_base"),
196:         ("gpt-3.5", "cl100k_base"),
197:         ("o1", "o200k_base"),
198:         ("o3", "o200k_base"),
199:         # o4 reasoning models use o200k_base; without this they fell through to
200:         # the cl100k_base default.
201:         ("o4", "o200k_base"),
202:     ):
203:         if model.startswith(prefix):
204:             return encoding
205: 
206:     return DEFAULT_ENCODING

209: class TiktokenCounter(BaseTokenizer):
210:     """Token counter using tiktoken (OpenAI's tokenizer).
211: 
212:     This is the most accurate tokenizer for OpenAI models and provides
213:     a good approximation for many other models that use similar BPE
214:     tokenization.
215: 
216:     Example:
217:         counter = TiktokenCounter("gpt-4o")
218:         tokens = counter.count_text("Hello, world!")
219:         print(f"Token count: {tokens}")
220:     """
221: 
222:     # OpenAI-specific message overhead
223:     MESSAGE_OVERHEAD = 3
224:     REPLY_OVERHEAD = 3
225: 
226:     def __init__(self, model: str = "gpt-4o", encoding: str | None = None):
227:         """Initialize tiktoken counter.
228: 
229:         Args:
230:             model: Model name to determine encoding.
231:                    Defaults to 'gpt-4o' (o200k_base encoding).
232:             encoding: Explicit tiktoken encoding name (e.g. 'o200k_base') that
233:                    overrides model-based resolution. Used to price
234:                    private-tokenizer models (Claude) against a real BPE proxy
235:                    instead of a character estimate.
236:         """
237:         self.model = model
238:         self.encoding_name = encoding or get_encoding_for_model(model)
239:         self._encoding = None  # Lazy load
240:         self._count_cache = TokenCountCache()
241: 
242:     @property
243:     def encoding(self):
244:         """Lazy-load the encoding."""
245:         if self._encoding is None:
246:             self._encoding = _get_encoding(self.encoding_name)
247:         return self._encoding
248: 
249:     def count_text(self, text: str) -> int:
250:         """Count tokens in text using tiktoken.
251: 
252:         Args:
253:             text: Text to tokenize.
254: 
255:         Returns:
256:             Number of tokens.
257:         """
258:         if not text:
259:             return 0
260:         cached = self._count_cache.get(text)
261:         if cached is not None:
262:             return cached
263:         count = self._count_text_uncached(text)
264:         self._count_cache.put(text, count)
265:         return count
266: 
267:     def _count_text_uncached(self, text: str) -> int:
268:         try:
269:             return len(self.encoding.encode(text))
270:         except ValueError:
271:             # Passthrough content can legitimately contain strings that look
272:             # like tiktoken special tokens (e.g. "<|endoftext|>" or FIM markers
273:             # in code/tool output). Treat them as ordinary text instead of
274:             # raising, which would otherwise abort token counting for the whole
275:             # request. Matches AnthropicTokenCounter.count_text.
276:             return len(self.encoding.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
277: 
278:     def count_messages(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
279:         """Count tokens in messages using OpenAI's exact formula.
280: 
281:         This matches OpenAI's token counting for chat completions.
282: 
283:         Args:
284:             messages: List of chat messages.
285: 
286:         Returns:
287:             Total token count.
288:         """
289:         total = 0
290: 
291:         for message in messages:
292:             # Every message has overhead for role and formatting
293:             total += self.MESSAGE_OVERHEAD
294: 
295:             for key, value in message.items():
296:                 if value is None:
297:                     continue
298: 
299:                 if key == "content":
300:                     if isinstance(value, str):
301:                         total += self.count_text(value)
302:                     elif isinstance(value, list):
303:                         # Multi-part content
304:                         for part in value:
305:                             if isinstance(part, dict):
306:                                 if part.get("type") == "text":
307:                                     total += self.count_text(part.get("text", ""))
308:                                 elif part.get("type") == "image_url":
309:                                     # Image tokens vary by detail level
310:                                     detail = part.get("image_url", {}).get("detail", "auto")
311:                                     if detail == "low":
312:                                         total += 85
313:                                     else:
314:                                         total += 170  # Base for high detail
315:                                 else:
316:                                     total += self.count_text(str(part))
317:                             elif isinstance(part, str):
318:                                 total += self.count_text(part)
319:                 elif key == "role":
320:                     total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(value))
321:                 elif key == "name":
322:                     total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(value))
323:                     total += 1  # Name adds 1 token
324:                 elif key == "tool_calls":
325:                     for tool_call in value or []:
326:                         total += 3  # Tool call overhead
327:                         if "function" in tool_call:
328:                             func = tool_call["function"] or {}
329:                             total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(func.get("name")))
330:                             total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(func.get("arguments")))
331:                         if "id" in tool_call:
332:                             total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(tool_call["id"]))
333:                 elif key == "tool_call_id":
334:                     total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(value))
335:                 elif key == "function_call":
336:                     value = value or {}
337:                     total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(value.get("name")))
338:                     total += self.count_text(coerce_countable_text(value.get("arguments")))
339: 
340:         # Every reply is primed with assistant
341:         total += self.REPLY_OVERHEAD
342: 
343:         return total
344: 
345:     def encode(self, text: str) -> list[int]:
346:         """Encode text to token IDs.
347: 
348:         Args:
349:             text: Text to encode.
350: 
351:         Returns:
352:             List of token IDs.
353:         """
354:         try:
355:             return self.encoding.encode(text)
356:         except ValueError:
357:             # See count_text: literal special-token strings in passthrough
358:             # content must be encoded as ordinary text, not rejected. The
359:             # round-trip through decode() is unaffected.
360:             return self.encoding.encode(text, disallowed_special=())
361: 
362:     def decode(self, tokens: list[int]) -> str:
363:         """Decode token IDs to text.
364: 
365:         Args:
366:             tokens: List of token IDs.
367: 
368:         Returns:
369:             Decoded text.
370:         """
371:         return self.encoding.decode(tokens)
372: 
373:     def __repr__(self) -> str:
374:         return f"TiktokenCounter(model={self.model!r}, encoding={self.encoding_name!r})"

434: # Traffic Learner
435: # =============================================================================

438: class TrafficLearner:
439:     """Extracts learnable patterns from live proxy traffic.
440: 
441:     Operates entirely on rule-based heuristics — no LLM calls.
442:     Designed to be called from the proxy request/response path
443:     with minimal overhead (async, non-blocking).
444:     """
445: 
446:     def __init__(
447:         self,
448:         backend: LocalBackend | None = None,
449:         user_id: str = "default",
450:         agent_type: str = "unknown",
451:         max_history: int = 20,
452:         dedup_window: int = 100,
453:         min_evidence: int = 5,
454:         max_pending_patterns: int = 2048,
455:     ) -> None:
456:         """Initialize the traffic learner.
457: 
458:         Args:
459:             backend: Memory backend to save patterns to. If None, patterns
460:                 are accumulated but not persisted until a backend is set.
461:             user_id: Default user ID for saved memories.
462:             agent_type: Which coding agent is being wrapped (claude, codex, gemini, etc.).
463:                 Used to determine the correct output file for flushing patterns.
464:             max_history: Number of recent tool calls to keep for pattern matching.
465:             dedup_window: Number of recent pattern hashes to track for dedup.
466:             min_evidence: Minimum times a pattern must be seen before saving.
467:         """
468:         self._backend = backend
469:         self._user_id = user_id
470:         self.agent_type = agent_type
471:         self._max_history = max_history
472:         self._min_evidence = min_evidence
473:         self._max_pending_patterns = max_pending_patterns
474: 
475:         # Recent tool call history for error→recovery matching
476:         self._tool_history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
477: 
478:         # Pattern accumulator: hash → (pattern, count). LRU-ordered and capped:
479:         # a pattern that is seen once but never reaches ``min_evidence`` would
480:         # otherwise linger here forever, so this dict grew unbounded over a
481:         # long-lived proxy's traffic (the sibling ``_saved_hashes`` is trimmed
482:         # to ``dedup_window`` for the same reason; this one was missed). Evicting
483:         # the least-recently-corroborated pending pattern is safe: if it recurs
484:         # it simply restarts accumulation.
485:         self._pattern_counts: OrderedDict[str, tuple[ExtractedPattern, int]] = OrderedDict()
486: 
487:         # Dedup: hashes of patterns already saved to DB
488:         self._saved_hashes: set[str] = set()
489:         # content_hash → memory.id for persisted rows. Lets re-sightings
490:         # bump the existing row's evidence_count instead of creating a
491:         # duplicate row.
492:         self._persisted_ids: dict[str, str] = {}
493:         self._dedup_window = dedup_window
494: 
495:         # Stats
496:         self._patterns_extracted = 0
497:         self._patterns_saved = 0
498:         self._requests_processed = 0
499: 
500:         # Background save queue
501:         self._save_queue: asyncio.Queue[ExtractedPattern] = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=100)
502:         self._save_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
503:         self._stopping = False
504: 
505:         # Dirty-flag debounced flush to CLAUDE.md / MEMORY.md. Set whenever
506:         # a pattern is accumulated; checked by _flush_worker.
507:         self._flush_dirty = False
508:         self._last_flush_at = 0.0
509:         self._flush_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
510: 
511:         # Cached project roots discovered via the learn plugin registry.
512:         # Populated lazily in flush_to_file.
513:         self._project_roots_cache: list[ProjectInfo] | None = None
514: 
515:     # =========================================================================
516:     # Public API
517:     # =========================================================================
518: 
519:     def set_backend(self, backend: LocalBackend) -> None:
520:         """Set or update the memory backend."""
521:         self._backend = backend
522: 
523:     async def start(self) -> None:
524:         """Start the background save worker and flush worker."""
525:         # Hydrate persisted dedup state before workers spin up so cross-session
526:         # re-sightings bump existing rows instead of creating duplicates.
527:         await self._hydrate_persisted_state()
528:         if self._save_task is None or self._save_task.done():
529:             self._save_task = asyncio.create_task(self._save_worker())
530:         if self._flush_task is None or self._flush_task.done():
531:             self._flush_task = asyncio.create_task(self._flush_worker())
532: 
533:     async def stop(self) -> None:
534:         """Stop the background workers, drain the save queue, final flush."""
535:         self._stopping = True
536: 
537:         if self._flush_task and not self._flush_task.done():
538:             self._flush_task.cancel()
539:             try:
540:                 await self._flush_task
541:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
542:                 pass
543: 
544:         # Drain any remaining patterns in the queue before cancelling
545:         if self._save_task and not self._save_task.done():
546:             self._save_task.cancel()
547:             try:
548:                 await self._save_task
549:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
550:                 pass
551: 
552:         # Drain any patterns left in the queue (worker may have been cancelled mid-flight)
553:         while not self._save_queue.empty():
554:             try:
555:                 pattern = self._save_queue.get_nowait()
556:                 if self._backend is not None:
557:                     await self._backend.save_memory(
558:                         content=pattern.content,
559:                         user_id=self._user_id,
560:                         importance=pattern.importance,
561:                         metadata={
562:                             "source": "traffic_learner",
563:                             "category": pattern.category.value,
564:                             "evidence_count": pattern.evidence_count,
565:                             **pattern.metadata,
566:                         },
567:                     )
568:                     self._patterns_saved += 1
569:             except Exception:
570:                 break
571: 
572:         # Final flush on shutdown — bypass debounce.
573:         await self.flush_to_file()
574: 
575:     async def _flush_worker(self) -> None:
576:         """Background worker: call flush_to_file when dirty, rate-limited."""
577:         while True:
578:             try:
579:                 await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
580:                 if not self._flush_dirty:
581:                     continue
582:                 if time.monotonic() - self._last_flush_at < FLUSH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS:
583:                     continue
584:                 # Reset before flushing so patterns accumulated during the
585:                 # flush still trigger a follow-up.
586:                 self._flush_dirty = False
587:                 self._last_flush_at = time.monotonic()
588:                 await self.flush_to_file()
589:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
590:                 break
591:             except Exception as e:
592:                 logger.warning("Traffic learner flush worker iteration failed: %s", e)
593: 
594:     async def flush_to_file(self) -> None:
595:         """Flush patterns (persisted + in-memory) to agent-native context files.
596: 
597:         Buckets patterns by project via longest-matching file path in content
598:         or entity_refs, routes by category to CLAUDE.md vs MEMORY.md, and
599:         delegates the actual write to the learn plugin writer.
600: 
601:         Un-anchored patterns (no absolute path in content) are dropped in v1.
602:         """
603:         try:
604:             from headroom.learn.registry import auto_detect_plugins, get_plugin
605:         except Exception as e:
606:             logger.debug("Traffic learner flush: learn package unavailable (%s)", e)
607:             return
608: 
609:         # Resolve plugin: explicit agent_type wins, else first detected plugin.
610:         try:
611:             if self.agent_type and self.agent_type != "unknown":
612:                 plugin = get_plugin(self.agent_type)
613:             else:
614:                 detected = auto_detect_plugins()
615:                 if not detected:
616:                     logger.debug("Traffic learner flush: no agent plugins detected")
617:                     return
618:                 plugin = detected[0]
619:         except KeyError:
620:             logger.debug("No learn plugin for agent_type=%s", self.agent_type)
621:             return
622: 
623:         # Gather patterns: persisted rows + in-memory accumulator, deduped.
624:         patterns = self._collect_all_patterns()
625:         if not patterns:
626:             return
627: 
628:         # Evidence gate: require self._min_evidence corroborations to flush,
629:         # including at shutdown. One-shot singletons are noise, not signal.
630:         patterns = [p for p in patterns if p.evidence_count >= self._min_evidence]
631:         if not patterns:
632:             return
633: 
634:         # Drop A→B / B→A contradictions among error_recovery patterns.
635:         # Both directions appearing with enough evidence usually means
636:         # opposite-direction typos in different sessions, not stable advice.
637:         patterns = _drop_contradictions(patterns)

1: """Memory integration handler for the proxy server.
2: 
3: This module provides memory capabilities for the Headroom proxy:
4: 1. MemoryHandler - Unified handler for memory operations
5:    - inject_tools() - Add memory tools to requests
6:    - search_and_format_context() - Search memories, format for injection
7:    - has_memory_tool_calls() - Detect memory tool usage in response
8:    - handle_memory_tool_calls() - Execute tools, return results
9: 
10: Usage:
11:     config = MemoryConfig(enabled=True, backend="local")
12:     handler = MemoryHandler(config)
13: 
14:     # Inject tools into request
15:     tools, was_injected = handler.inject_tools(existing_tools, "anthropic")
16: 
17:     # Search and inject context
18:     context = await handler.search_and_format_context(user_id, messages)
19: 
20:     # Handle tool calls in response
21:     if handler.has_memory_tool_calls(response, "anthropic"):
22:         results = await handler.handle_memory_tool_calls(response, user_id, "anthropic")
23: """
24: 
25: from __future__ import annotations
26: 
27: import asyncio
28: import enum
29: import inspect
30: import json
31: import logging
32: import os
33: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
34: from datetime import datetime, timezone
35: from pathlib import Path
36: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal
37: 
38: from headroom.memory import qdrant_env
39: from headroom.memory.storage_router import (
40:     BackendRouter,
41:     BackendRouterConfig,
42:     MemoryStorageMode,
43:     RequestContext,
44:     ResolvedScope,
45: )
46: 
47: if TYPE_CHECKING:
48:     from headroom.memory.backends.local import LocalBackend
49: 
50: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
51: 
52: 
53: class MemoryMode(str, enum.Enum):
54:     """Memory injection mode (PR-B6).
55: 
56:     AUTO_TAIL (default): Memory retrieval runs at request entry; results are
57:     appended to the latest user message tail (the live zone). The cache hot
58:     zone (system prompt / instructions / frozen prefix) is never mutated —
59:     invariant I2 from PR-A2.
60: 
61:     TOOL: Auto-injection is disabled entirely. The model calls the
62:     ``memory_search`` tool explicitly when it wants memory; retrieval runs in
63:     the tool execution path, not the prompt-construction path. Memory becomes
64:     opt-in (and visible to the model) rather than implicit.
65: 
66:     See REALIGNMENT/04-phase-B-live-zone.md PR-B6 for the rationale.
67:     """
68: 
69:     AUTO_TAIL = "auto_tail"
70:     TOOL = "tool"
71: 
72: 
73: # Memory tool names for detection (Headroom's custom tools)
74: MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES = {
75:     "memory_save",
76:     "memory_search",
77:     "memory_update",
78:     "memory_delete",
79:     "memory_list",
80: }
81: 
82: # Anthropic's native memory tool name
83: NATIVE_MEMORY_TOOL_NAME = "memory"
84: 
85: # Beta header required for native memory tool
86: NATIVE_MEMORY_BETA_HEADER = "context-management-2025-06-27"
87: 
88: # Native memory tool type
89: NATIVE_MEMORY_TOOL_TYPE = "memory_20250818"
90: 
91: # Maximum time to wait for a single backend initialization (one-shot).
92: # Applies to MemoryHandler._ensure_initialized. On timeout, _initialized
93: # stays False so that subsequent requests retry instead of deadlocking.
94: # See wiki/plans/2026-04-17-fix-codex-proxy-resilience-plan.md "Risks" row 7.
95: STARTUP_INIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0
96: 
97: 
98: def _serialize_created_at(value: Any) -> str | None:
99:     """Best-effort timestamp serialization for tool-result payloads.
100: 
101:     The backend may return ``datetime`` (from a freshly-saved row) or
102:     string (from a hydrated SQLite row). Either way the model needs
103:     a string to render in chat. Unparseable values → None.
104:     """
105:     if value is None:
106:         return None
107:     if isinstance(value, str):
108:         return value
109:     if hasattr(value, "isoformat"):
110:         try:
111:             iso = value.isoformat()
112:             return iso if isinstance(iso, str) else str(iso)
113:         except Exception:
114:             return str(value)
115:     return str(value)
